newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply lower on fund sales.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply lower on fund sales.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended sharply lower Tuesday on renewed fund selling prompted by a surging dollar, a modest increase in December US CPI inflation, and fears of further central bank gold sales, traders said.

"The US dollar is strong, as are equity markets, and with the US annual CPI core inflation rate so low, there's no reason for metals to rally," said Anthony Raia of Linnco Futures Group in Chicago. "The market is heading lower."
In data released Tuesday, the US CPI ex-food and energy only rose 2.6 pct in 1996, the smallest rise since 1994.
Meanwhile, the US dollar saw a 30-month high against the mark Tuesday, while the S&P500 equity index saw a new all-time high.
COMEX February gold ended down $5.00 an ounce at $354.70, after a late sell off by funds saw a new life-of-contract low at $354.00. Total estimated gold futures volume was 65,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended was quoted $353.70/20, a new three-year low, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $357.40, and the New York close Monday at $358.30/70.
While physical demand remains robust, investment demand for gold remains weak, analysts said.

"Prospects for low inflation, attractive returns from paper assets and supply pressure from central banks and producers continue to heighten bearish sentiment," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
On Monday the Dutch central bank said it sold 300 tonnes of gold, about one fifth of its reserves, and an amount equivalent to about two thirds of South Africa's annual gold mine production.

"The statement Monday by Bundesbank president Tietmeyer that there would be no further G-10 gold sales for the time being was very tentative and there is already talk that there are other European central banks in the market," one bullion banker said.
"If the European central banks want to hold a firesale of their gold reserves ahead of EMU (European monetary union) then the market is only going lower," he said.
Gold was weaker than silver Tuesday, with the spot gold/silver ratio slipping to 75.90 from 76.23 Monday.

COMEX March silver ended down 4.2 cents an ounce at $4.675, after seeing an intraday low at $4.670, though March silver remained above the contract low set on January 6 at $4.635. The March/May silver spread widened to 5.0 cents from 4.5 cents at Monday's close.
Gold was weaker than platinum also Tuedsay, with the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread widening to $9.10 an ounce from $5.10 an ounce at Monday's close.
NYMEX April platinum ended down $1.20 an ounce, closing on its session lows at $365.50.
"Weakness in gold and ample supply continue to pressure (platinum) prices", Rinehimer said.

"Expansion of the Stillwater mine in the U.S. and the expected mid-year start-up of the Hartley Platinum mine in Zimbabwe will add to 1997 supply, while accelerating growth and expansion of advance technologies should support increased demand for platinum.

"Despite some decline in platinum usage in autocatalysts in Europe, the U.S. and Japan, increased platinum demand is expected from the developing auto markets of Asia and Latin America due to higher vehicle production and stricter clean air legislation.
NYMEX March palladium ended down $1.70 at $123.50.
